items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: Because Gleason and Williams, because they'd been to Columbia and knew that scene, got me a tremendous writeup in the magazine there

ctx.x: But meanwhile, none of the jazz people - None of them are coming in. None. None of them are coming in. They're waiting for 10:00 to come in. At 10:00, -- 9:00 we're through, we got one hour, we got lockers downstairs. Well, by that time, that's lunchtime, if you know what I mean. Everybody has got his own little taste in his own locker, and we're all ready. And you go down there and you get all ready and you relax and you forget about those two hours you just had.

And you're ready. And you come up there and you hit Muskrat or whatever you want to play, and the house is full. Because Gleason and Williams, because they'd been to Columbia and knew that scene, got me a tremendous writeup in the magazine there, and we had all those college kids coming in. Columbia was next door -- to hear this. And what the management did not know was -- or didn't seem to know, although it was their place, was that although they come in through the front door, there was no trick at all for them…
